Hi Lydia / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — good conversation on usage patterns and where Nimbus expects burst growth next year. Per our chat, attached is a focused proposal that gives you flexibility to keep current SKUs for core workflows while shifting incremental consumption to a pooled, usage-style bucket with rollover credits. High level:

- Term: 12 month renewal (starts 2027-01-01) with optional 6-month rollover for unused pooled consumption.
- Option 1 (Conservative): 10% uplift on current committed units + pooled consumption bucket (30k units/month) with 6-month rollover.
- Option 2 (Aggressive): Move 40% of current seats to consumption pricing (lower per-unit rate), commit to 12 months; we price this at a blended 8% uplift vs current annualized spend.
- Tradeoff: we can add a one-time 10% credit applied to Q1 invoice if Nimbus signs by 2026-11-12 (this locks current GPU/instance mix).

Notes and clarifications in the attachment (SKU-MAPPING-and-credits.xlsx). The PDF walks through example invoices and how the rollover credit flows if you underuse the pooled bucket.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You pick Option 1 or 2 (or mark questions inline in the spreadsheet).
2) If you want legal review, we can spin a tracked amendment for signatures — I can send a DocuSign link to speed approvals.
3) If you prefer, we can book a 30-min follow-up (I included Jordan on CC to answer any billing/pricing mechanics).

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow afternoon PST.

Thanks,

--

Hi Lydia — thanks for the quick list of questions, great points. See answers inline and attached updated pricing table (v2):

1) Rollover mechanics (Option 1): pooled units that roll over retain their classification as pooled consumption credits for up to 6 months. They do not convert into named-seat licenses. If you consistently want to convert to seats we can add a conversion clause at a pre-agreed price (see row 18 in the spreadsheet).

2) Blended rate example (Option 2): for a 100k monthly inference-unit run rate, the blended per-unit goes from $0.0028 (current seat-equivalent proxy) to $0.0022 under the consumption conversion (approx -21% unit delta) once you shift 40% of seat-hours into the pooled bucket. I included worked examples on page 3 of the PDF.

3) The one-time 10% credit applies to the first invoice after the amendment becomes effective and will be applied to net invoice (post usage accounting) — we will show the credit line as a separate line item; accounting teams usually treat that as a contra-invoice credit.

I attached the updated PDF and SKU spreadsheet (both attached). To accelerate procurement and lock the instance mix/pricing we can issue the amendment via DocuSign. If Nimbus signs by 2026-11-12, we will also add the one-time credit line to the amendment.
